theory_title: Cashless and reimbursement, and why it matters
theory_content: Cashless treatment means the insurer settles directly with a network hospital; reimbursement means you pay and claim back, often waiting weeks with a large bill already on your card. Check the network list before you need it, and keep the policy number somewhere a family member can find it. The process is difficult precisely when you are least able to manage it.

theory_title: Moving insurers without losing your waiting period
theory_content: Health policies can be ported to another insurer at renewal while carrying forward the waiting periods you have already served. Apply at least 45 days before renewal. Without portability, switching would reset a four-year pre-existing-disease wait, which is what traps people in policies that have become expensive or unhelpful.

theory_title: The risks that are not death
theory_content: Term cover pays if you die. It pays nothing if you survive a heart attack and cannot work for two years — which is statistically more likely. A critical illness rider pays a lump sum on diagnosis, and disability cover replaces income. For a single earner with dependants, these fill a gap that life cover structurally cannot.

theory_title: The policy that was right five years ago
theory_content: Cover needs change with income, dependants and debt. A ₹50 lakh term policy bought before a home loan and a child is no longer adequate. Review after any major life event, and buy additional term cover rather than surrendering and repurchasing — premiums rise with age and any condition diagnosed since.
